outcome: attitudes and beliefs regarding umbilical cord clamping practices
preferred approach to cord clamping (event-based vs. time-based)
cohort: Healthcare professionals in Sweden, including midwives, nursing staff, obstetricians, and pediatricians/neonatologists, who responded to a national electronic survey.
finding: While timing of cord clamping is generally considered important, significant interprofessional variations exist in attitudes and preferred approaches among Swedish healthcare professionals, especially in scenarios involving neonatal resuscitation and elective cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Among obstetricians, 28.8% reported considering an event-based approach to cord clamping in elective cesarean sections.
